text: Start with four columns: Backlog, Ready, Doing, and Done. Each card states a concrete next step. Backlog ideas may be unassigned; moving a card to Ready requires one owner so both people know who will move it forward.

Start with four columns: Backlog, Ready, Doing, and Done. Each card states a concrete next step. Backlog ideas may be unassigned; moving a card to Ready requires one owner so both people know who will move it forward.Mark blocked cards with the reason, the person or event needed to unblock them, and a follow-up date. Keep the task owner responsible for follow-up, and provide a waiting-on-me filter so either teammate can quickly find requests needing their help.

Backlog ideas may be unassigned; moving a card to Ready requires one owner so both people know who will move it forward.Mark blocked cards with the reason, the person or event needed to unblock them, and a follow-up date. Keep the task owner responsible for follow-up, and provide a waiting-on-me filter so either teammate can quickly find requests needing their help.Hold a brief weekly review to choose upcoming work and revisit overdue blockers. For each stalled task, decide whether to follow up, change the approach, or drop it. Try this setup for two weeks, then adjust whichever part creates confusion or unnecessary upkeep.
